parties:
Mustafa Jaglul Wahed ------- Petitioner.
Vs.
Authorised Officer, Ministry of Public Works and Urban Development ------- Respondents
full_judgment:
3. Respondent No. 1 has asserted that the property in question was an abandoned property and it stood vested in the Government. During the recent Revisional Settlement Operation in 1975 the property was recorded in D.P. Khatian the name of the Ministry of Public Works and Urban Development as an abandoned property. The Khatian is Annexure-1 to the affidavit-in-opposition. One Golam Mustafa, a Manager of Janata Bank Branch at 78, Nawabpur Road, Dacca, was in possession of the 1st floor of the house in question as a tenant. The Bank had full knowledge that the owner was not in Bangladesh. Mr. Nurul Huda's son Mr. Qamrul Huda, a Deputy General Manager at the Head Office of the Janata Bank, had knowledge that the property was not in the management of Malibul Rahman Siddiqui. He got the Money , Suit instituted on 15.11.72 and it was decreed ex parte on 15.11.72. The execution case was filed in hot haste on 21.11.72. The auction for sale was held on 24.2.73 and the sale was confirmed on 27.3.73. It has been alleged that the Power of Attorney by the petitioner was executed and registered on 27.4.73 with the malafide intention to grab the property. Subsequently Mr. Golam Mustafa was transferred at the instance of Mr. Quamrul Huda and Mr. Nurul Huda was inducted illegally in the first-floor of the premises. The Money Execution Case were proceeded illegally and the alleged auction purchaser did never get deli-very of possession. The ground floor of the house continued to remain in possession of one Dr. Delwar Hossain Chowdhury of 32/2, Azimpur Road. Dacca who reportedly went into part possession of the house in pursuance of an alleged agreement dated 26.1.1971 for sale, purportedly made with the owner. Dr. Delwar Hossain Chowdhury let out the ground floor to M/S Hysons and Company for accommodation of its Officers and thereafter M/S. Hysons vacated the ground-floor of the house. It was reported by Respondent No. 4 that the ground floor was let out to him on 15.12.78. The impugned notice was legally issued for asking the illegal occupants to surrender their illegal possession to the Government. The allegations of the petitioners as to the manner of eviction have been denied as false and concocted by respondent No. 1. According to Respondent No. 1, Mr. Nurul Huda was at Dacca on the date of eviction and he sent his son Ajmal Huda to receive his belongings on his behalf as per inventory made by the Authorised Officer. All moveable properties of Mr. Huda were received by his son who signed without any objection of the list of goods (Annexure 'III' to the affidavit-in opposition). The Government or the Ministry of Public Works and Urban Development was not made a party in the Money Suit of Money Execution Case. Prior to notice dated 7.12.72, another dated 18.8.78 had earlier been served upon Mr. Nurul Huda directing him to satisfy the Ministry within 7 days under what basis he was occupying the house. A similar notice was issued on 16.11.78 and served upon the occupant. Another notice dated 24.12.79 was served upon Mr. Nurul Huda to appear before the Authorised Officer but he did not appear. Lastly on 18.1.80 Mr. Huda was served with a notice that he would be evicted on 19.1.80. The eviction was done in accordance with law. Thereafter, the ground floor of the house was alloted to the Subordinate Judge, 1st. Court Dacca and the first floor was alloted to respondent No. 4. Neither Mukhlesur Rahman Shariff nor his predecessor-in possession of the ground floor of the house, M/S. Hysons and Company, was a tenant of the petitioner. 

 6. In the affidavit-in-reply the petitioner has stated that the record of the D.P. khatian relates to some other persons and to some other property. The delivery of possession was taken through Court. By a supplementary-affidavit the petitioner filed several papers. Annexure 'P' of the Khatian shows that the property was recorded in 1971 in the name of the petitioner. Annexure '0' is the rent receipt dated 24.9.73. Ann-exure 'R' shows that on 11.10.73 the petitioner's name was mutated in the records of Dacca Paurashava. Annexure 'X', a certified copy of the orders dated 19.9.72 and 6.10.72 of Money Suit No. 59 of 1979, shows the Registration of the case and the service of summons upon Mujibur Rahman Shariff and other defendants. Annexure ‘Y' is a certified copy of Order No. 16 dated 30.6.74 of the Money Execution case No. 35 of 1972 which reads:-"Writ of possession was duly executed. Put up on 3.7.73 for order". As the present petition was filed by the Constituted Attorney of the petitioner the respondent challenged the identity of petitioner. Mostafa Jaglul Wahed, the petitioner, himself filed an affidavit affirming that be authorised and empowered his constituted Attorney Khandker Abdul Bari to file this petition. He was presented and identified before us by Mr. Shafiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate who has also appeared in his case. 

 11. The description of the property in question given in the Certificate of Sale (Annexure 'S' to the petition) does not, on the face of it, agree with the record of the D.P. Khatian, (Annexure to the affidavit-in-opposition). Further evidence is required for the identification. There is no disclosure in the affidavit-in-opposition at whose instance the record was made. Though the Khatian was recorded on 21.10.75 in the name of the Ministry of Works, respondent No. 1 did not act on it. Much later from a joint survey report dated 3.12.79 respondent No. 1 came to know about the actual state of affairs. Thereafter it acted on that report, issued notice and ultimately evicted the petitioner's tenant. Though there are references in the affidavit-in opposition to the earlier notices dated 18.8.78, and 16.11.78, it appears that the Government did not pursue the matter in 1978. The petitioner has challenged those notices as spurious and asserted that they had never been served on his tenant.
